body:
Hi,

example celery run command 
```bash
celery -A celery_main worker \
    --loglevel INFO \
    --without-gossip \
    --without-mingle \
    -O fair \
    -P eventlet \
    -c 10
```

I get the same error on Ubuntu 20.04.1 with Celery 5.0.0 upgrade.
Problem also occurs when using `--app`

I am passing App as first parameter after the celery binary:
```
ExecStart=/bin/sh -c '${CELERY_BIN} -A ${CELERY_APP} multi start ${CELERYD_NODES} \
  --pidfile=${CELERYD_PID_FILE} \
  --logfile=${CELERYD_LOG_FILE} --loglevel=${CELERYD_LOG_LEVEL} ${CELERYD_OPTS}'
```
Ignore my previous comment here, apparently when I tried that it was erroneously with 4.4.7

I had the same problem in celery beat
```
celery v4.4.7 :
celery beat -A celery_main --loglevel=info

celery v5.0.0 :
celery -A celery_main beat -s celerybeat-schedule.db --loglevel INFO
```
Apparently, they've migrated argument parsing to shitty Click in v5 and that's causing a lot of troubles...

body:
@ozkansen @mfonville thanks for the report. I am trying the following command with commit 9b5f6f5531f45525e904cef114d653a93f1c9635 and it seems to work:

```
$ celery -A proj multi start worker1 --pidfile=tmp/celery.pid --logfile=tmp/celery.log
```

Maybe I am missing something though. Please let us know if you manage to try this with a more recent release!

@georgepsarakis I also have the same issue. I tried running `celery -A proj multi --verbose start 1  --pidfile="pid/%n.pid" --logfile="log/%n.log"` and the resulting worker command is `/proj/.venv/bin/python3 -m celery worker --detach --pidfile=pid/celery1.pid --logfile=log/celery1.log -n celery1@mimas --executable=/proj/.venv/bin/python3` in which the project is not included. 

I use celery version 5.0.0 downloaded from PyPI.
When executing the `multi` command it returns "OK" but the worker command doesn't receive the application so it cannot start

Same here and  just the simple and old command:

**celery -A tasks worker**

and I've got:
**Error: Invalid value for -A / --app: No module named celery.five**

I had to go back to 4.4.7 to have everything working again 🤔

@thedrow 
> What's so shitty about it?

Please take a look at the number of [issues](https://github.com/pallets/click/issues?q=is:issue) (both open and closed) of the Click project. It's more than 1000. You don't think that it is too many for the simple argument parsing library, do you?

> And why do you have to diss on other people's efforts?

I'm not trying to diss on other people's efforts. I appreciate the work of all Celery team, seriously. Many people benefit from Celery all over the world (including myself). I'm just saying that switching to Click was a bad decision IMHO and the number of people having troubles after upgrading to v5 seems to prove that...

> > **celery -A tasks worker**
> > and I've got:

I fixed this issue for me as well with `pip install celery==4.4.7` and redeploying my app.

I can confirm that parsing option from a config file as described in the documentation works in 5.0,0. I got it working by adding all options hardcoded into my systemd service file.

The error in syslog: celery.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=2/INVALIDARGUMENT (when loading options from the config file).
